[LLM] node.exe spawning child_process targets — vm2 Promise species sandbox escape post-exploitation Exploitation Medium
Detects the post-escape pattern from CVE-2026-47208 PoC where the attacker uses ex.constructor.constructor('return process')().mainModule.require('child_process').execSync(...) to spawn arbitrary host processes from inside a vm2 sandbox. Filters for node.exe parent spawning shells/cmd/touch/curl/wget without a benign build-tool ancestor. Rationale: PoC ends in 'ex.constructor.constructor("return process")().mainModule.require(\'child_process\').execSync(\'touch pwned\')'. The detectable observable is node.exe parent spawning child_process targets without a benign npm/yarn/electron build-tool ancestor. Corroborated against TheHackerNews 2026 vm2 wave coverage and Kodem analysis of AI-agent RCE risk. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/patriksimek/vm2/security/advisories/GHSA-qvjj-29qf-hp7p • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/vm2-nodejs-library-vulnerabilities.html • https://www.kodemsecurity.com/resources/vm2-sandbox-escape-vulnerabilities-the-2026-cve-wave-turning-ai-agents-into-host-rce-vectors
ATT&CKT1068 T1059.007 T1059.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
// vm2 sandbox escape -> child_process.execSync spawns host process from node.exe
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","touch.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","npm ci","npm run","yarn install","pnpm install","node-gyp","electron-builder","husky","postinstall"))
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd  = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildPath  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd   = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256, ProcessIntegrityLevel
| order by Timestamp desc
// ASIM process-create — node.exe parent spawning shell/cmd/touch after vm2 escape
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName endswith "node.exe"
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","touch.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","certutil.exe")
| where not (ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","npm ci","npm run","yarn","pnpm","node-gyp","electron","postinstall","husky"))
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"

[LLM] vm2 Promise species sandbox escape PoC fingerprint in scripts/command lines Weaponization High
Hunts the specific JavaScript exploitation idiom from CVE-2026-47208 PoC: combinations of Symbol.species class extension of Promise, ex.constructor.constructor('return process')(), and mainModule.require('child_process'). These strings appear in attacker payloads delivered to vm2-using services and in saved exploit files. Rationale: The PoC contains highly distinctive idioms: 'ex.constructor.constructor("return process")()' for breaking out via the prototype chain, 'mainModule.require(\'child_process\')' for arbitrary execution, and 'Symbol.species' class extension of Promise — the actual vulnerable mechanism. These three strings together are extremely rare in benign code. Sigma omitted because the detection chains union/joins across cmdline and file telemetry — single-event shape doesn't fit. Corroborated against the GitHub advisory PoC and GitLab CVE-2026-24120 advisory of the same Promise.species root cause. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-76w7-j9cq-rx2j • https://advisories.gitlab.com/npm/vm2/CVE-2026-24120/ • https://github.com/patriksimek/vm2/security/advisories/GHSA-qvjj-29qf-hp7p
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1068

]);

[LLM] vm2 sandbox-escape PoC strings observed in inbound HTTP request body / WAF Exploitation High
Hunts the exact JavaScript token sequence from the CVE-2026-47131 PoC (Buffer.call.call/__lookupGetter__/__lookupSetter__ + WebAssembly.compileStreaming + e.constructor.constructor + mainModule.require) in web request URLs and bodies traversing the WAF / reverse proxy. Targets any service that hands user-supplied JS to a vm2 sandbox. Rationale: PoC body in the advisory cites the exact strings Buffer.call.call({}.__lookupGetter__, Buffer, "__proto__"), WebAssembly.compileStreaming(), e.constructor.constructor, and new HostFunction("return process")().mainModule.require("child_process").execSync — those tokens together don't appear in legitimate JSON payloads or REST API traffic. The narrow string set keeps FPs near zero. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-v6mx-mf47-r5wg • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-47131
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.007

| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("echo pwned","child_process","execSync")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

[LLM] Node.exe spawning OS shell after vm2 sandbox exploitation Installation High
Hunts the post-exploit signature of CVE-2026-47131: a Node.js process spawning cmd/powershell/bash/sh with command lines containing the PoC's distinctive 'echo pwned' marker or child_process.execSync invocations. Node legitimately shells out occasionally for build tooling, so we anchor on the PoC string and the unusual integrity-level / parent-tree combination. Rationale: The PoC ends with execSync("echo pwned", { stdio: "inherit" }) — a near-unique marker — preceded by mainModule.require("child_process"). The node→shell parent-child plus those two string tokens together is article-specific and won't fire on normal Node build steps. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-v6mx-mf47-r5wg

      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\bash.exe'

  condition: parent and child and cmdline

[LLM] Vulnerable vm2 package (<=3.11.3) present in Defender software inventory Weaponization Medium
Configuration-hygiene hunt that flags any managed host where Defender TVM has indexed an npm vm2 package at version 3.11.3 or earlier, the vulnerable range for CVE-2026-47131. Use this to drive patching outreach before an exploit attempt lands. Rationale: The advisory explicitly states 'Affected packages: npm:vm2 (vuln <= 3.11.3)' and assigns CVE-2026-47131. Defender TVM ingests npm package inventory from app-server hosts and emits a CveId match — the simplest article-specific hunt. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-v6mx-mf47-r5wg • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-47131

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-47131")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-47131")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"

| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Marimo CVE-2026-39987 /terminal/ws RCE: notebook process spawns shell or network tooling Exploitation High
Hunts the initial-access foothold described by Sysdig: an internet-reachable marimo notebook process (Python/uvicorn) spawns sh/bash/curl/wget/nc as a child of the unauthenticated /terminal/ws WebSocket exploit path. The marimo runtime should not be spawning shells or network egress utilities under normal load. Rationale: Anchors on the exact CVE-2026-39987 exploitation chain — marimo Python process spawning a shell/network utility through the unauthenticated /terminal/ws WebSocket. The parent-process predicate (marimo in cmdline of a Python/uvicorn parent) is the article-specific narrowing that distinguishes this from generic Python shellouts. Cross-checked with Sysdig blog and NVD entry confirming /terminal/ws is the exploit primitive. Cross-checked against: • https://webflow.sysdig.com/blog/ai-agent-at-the-wheel-how-an-attacker-used-llms-to-move-from-a-cve-to-an-internal-database-in-4-pivots • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-39987 • https://github.com/Nxploited/CVE-2026-39987
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python","python3","uvicorn","gunicorn","marimo")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "marimo"
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","curl","wget","ncat","nc","busybox")
    or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/bin/sh","bash -c","/dev/tcp/","import socket","import pty")
| where not(FileName in~ ("python","python3") and ProcessCommandLine has "marimo")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("python","python3","uvicorn","gunicorn","marimo")
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has "marimo"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("sh","bash","dash","curl","wget","ncat","nc","busybox")
    or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/bin/sh","bash -c","/dev/tcp/","import socket","import pty")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, Hash
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] AWS Secrets Manager GetSecretValue fan-out from multiple egress IPs Actions on Objectives High
Detects the LLM-agent fingerprint of replaying a single stolen IAM credential through a fanned-out egress pool: the same principal/access key calls GetSecretValue on the same secret from 3+ distinct source IPs in a short window — the IP diversification pattern Sysdig saw used to retrieve the SSH private key. Rationale: Targets the article's defining cloud-credential abuse signature: 'replayed them through a fanned-out egress pool to retrieve an SSH private key from AWS Secrets Manager.' The fan-out is the high-fidelity anomaly — legitimate apps call Secrets Manager from a stable set of IPs (NAT gateway, Lambda, EKS pod IP). The Datadog version also pins the five Cloudflare-egress IPs Sysdig observed. Sentinel/Defender empty: schema reference doesn't include AWSCloudTrail and Defender Advanced Hunting doesn't ingest CloudTrail. Cross-checked against: • https://webflow.sysdig.com/blog/ai-agent-at-the-wheel-how-an-attacker-used-llms-to-move-from-a-cve-to-an-internal-database-in-4-pivots • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/attackers-use-llm-agent-for-post.html
ATT&CKT1555.006 T1078.004

[LLM] SSH private key file enumeration then read (ls id_ed25519* → cat id_ed25519) Actions on Objectives High
Detects the LLM-agent value-handoff pattern Sysdig documented: an `ls -la ~/.ssh/id_ed25519*` existence check followed within seconds by `cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` on the same host/user. The list-then-read sequence on the exact same path is a strong indicator of programmatic (agent) operation, not a human reading the file directly. Rationale: Anchors on the exact behavioural fingerprint Sysdig called out as agent-confirmation: 'a cat command to print the contents of a specific file (cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519) is preceded by an ls command that passes the same file pattern as input (ls -la ~/.ssh/id_ed25519*) to confirm that the SSH Key exists.' The list-then-read within 60s, same user/host, is the high-fidelity tell — humans rarely script this; agents check existence before consumption. Cross-checked against: • https://webflow.sysdig.com/blog/ai-agent-at-the-wheel-how-an-attacker-used-llms-to-move-from-a-cve-to-an-internal-database-in-4-pivots
ATT&CKT1552.004 T1083

    | project ListTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, ListAccount = AccountName, ListCmd = ProcessCommandLine;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where FileName in~ ("cat","head","less","more")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"\.ssh/id_(ed25519|rsa|ecdsa)(?!\.pub)"
| join kind=inner ListEvents on DeviceId
| where AccountName == ListAccount
| where Timestamp between (ListTime .. ListTime + WindowSeconds * 1s)
| project ListTime, CatTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ListTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, ListCmd, CatCmd = ProcessCommandLine
| order by CatTime desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowSeconds = 60;
let ListEvents = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ActingProcessName =~ "ls"
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("id_ed25519","id_rsa","id_ecdsa",".ssh/id_")
    | project ListTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ListUser = ActorUsername, ListCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ActingProcessName in~ ("cat","head","less","more")

| project ListTime, CatTime = TimeGenerated,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', TimeGenerated, ListTime),
          DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ListCmd, CatCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by CatTime desc
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.name:(cat OR head OR less OR more) @process.command_line:(*".ssh/id_ed25519"* OR *".ssh/id_rsa"* OR *".ssh/id_ecdsa"*) -@process.command_line:*".pub"*

| delay := _time - ls_time

[LLM] LLM-agent shell fingerprint: machine-consumption flags in single command Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects the structural fingerprint Sysdig identified as LLM-agent-driven shell sessions: a single command line combining stderr discard (2>/dev/null), pager-disable (--no-pager / PAGER=cat / unset PAGER / | cat), and the literal '---' delimiter or bounded-output markers the agent uses to chunk results. Two-of-three present in one command line is a strong agent signal. Rationale: Sysdig's third agent-indicator: 'every command is designed for machine consumption, with each command separated by a --- delimiter, along with bounded output captures, disabling the less command, and discarding the error stream (stderr) to minimize noise.' Three independent unusual-for-humans flags in one command line is the rare-conjunction signal. Pager-disable + stderr-discard alone is noisy (sysadmins do this); adding the literal '---' echo cuts FPs sharply. Cross-checked against: • https://webflow.sysdig.com/blog/ai-agent-at-the-wheel-how-an-attacker-used-llms-to-move-from-a-cve-to-an-internal-database-in-4-pivots
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("bash","sh","dash","zsh","sshd") or FileName in~ ("bash","sh","dash","zsh")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "2>/dev/null"
| extend pagerDisabled = ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--no-pager","PAGER=cat","unset PAGER","unset LESS","| cat","|cat")
| extend delimiterEcho = ProcessCommandLine has_any ("echo ---","echo \"---\"","echo '---'","printf '---")
      or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"\s---\s"
| where pagerDisabled and delimiterEcho
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName in~ ("bash","sh","dash","zsh") or ParentProcessName in~ ("sshd","bash","sh")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "2>/dev/null"
| extend pagerDisabled = ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--no-pager","PAGER=cat","unset PAGER","unset LESS","| cat","|cat")
| extend delimiterEcho = ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("echo ---","echo \"---\"","echo '---'","printf '---")
      or ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"\s---\s"
| where pagerDisabled and delimiterEcho
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: LLM-Agent Shell Fingerprint (Machine-Consumption Flags in One Command)
id: 3d8e1f72-2a4b-4c9d-8e6f-5a7b9c1d2e3f
status: experimental
description: Detects the structural shell-command fingerprint Sysdig attributed to LLM-agent-driven post-exploitation — stderr discard + pager disable + literal '---' delimiter in a single command line.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/attackers-use-llm-agent-for-post.html
  - https://webflow.sysdig.com/blog/ai-agent-at-the-wheel-how-an-attacker-used-llms-to-move-from-a-cve-to-an-internal-database-in-4-pivots
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/29
tags:
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1027
  - attack.defense_evasion
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  shell_parent:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
  stderr_discard:
    CommandLine|contains: '2>/dev/null'
  pager_disable:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '--no-pager'
      - 'PAGER=cat'
      - 'unset PAGER'
      - 'unset LESS'
      - '| cat'
      - '|cat'
  delimiter_echo:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'echo ---'
      - "echo '---'"
      - 'echo "---"'
      - 'printf "---'
  condition: shell_parent and stderr_discard and pager_disable and delimiter_echo
falsepositives:
  - Hand-written shell scripts that intentionally chunk output (rare)
  - Power users with shell aliases that disable pager and discard stderr globally
level: medium
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.name:(bash OR sh OR dash OR zsh) @process.command_line:*"2>/dev/null"* AND (@process.command_line:*"--no-pager"* OR @process.command_line:*"PAGER=cat"* OR @process.command_line:*"unset PAGER"* OR @process.command_line:*"| cat"*) AND (@process.command_line:*"echo ---"* OR @process.command_line:*"echo '---'"* OR @process.command_line:*"echo \"---\""*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\/(bash|sh|dash|zsh)$/i CommandLine=/2>\/dev\/null/i
| CommandLine=/(--no-pager|PAGER=cat|unset PAGER|unset LESS|\| cat|\|cat)/i
| CommandLine=/(echo ['\"]?---|printf ['\"]?---| --- )/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("bash","sh","dash","zsh") AND Processes.process="*2>/dev/null*" AND (Processes.process="*--no-pager*" OR Processes.process="*PAGER=cat*" OR Processes.process="*unset PAGER*" OR Processes.process="*| cat*" OR Processes.process="*|cat*" OR Processes.process="*unset LESS*") AND (Processes.process="*echo ---*" OR Processes.process="*echo \"---\"*" OR Processes.process="*echo '---'*" OR Processes.process="* --- *") by host Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
[LLM] Chinese-language LLM planning comment leaked into command stream (看还能做什么) Actions on Objectives High
Detects the specific Chinese-language planning comment 看还能做什么 ('See what else we can do') that Sysdig observed leaking from the LLM agent's internal reasoning directly into the executed shell command stream. Trivial implementation, very high fidelity — this exact string in a command line is essentially zero-FP outside of native-Chinese-speaking ops environments. Rationale: Quoted verbatim from the article: 'a Chinese-language planning comment, 看还能做什么 translating to See what else we can do leaked directly in the command stream when executing a credential search.' This is an exact-string IOC — zero false positives outside of environments with Chinese-language ops/scripts, and even there the precise five-character planning idiom is incongruous in shell commands. Cross-checked against: • https://webflow.sysdig.com/blog/ai-agent-at-the-wheel-how-an-attacker-used-llms-to-move-from-a-cve-to-an-internal-database-in-4-pivots
ATT&CKT1059
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
union DeviceProcessEvents, DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "看还能做什么"
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "看还能做什么"
   or AdditionalFields contains "看还能做什么"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImProcessCreate | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where ActingProcessCommandLine contains "看还能做什么" or ParentProcessCommandLine contains "看还能做什么" | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, CmdLine = ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentCmdLine = ParentProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate"),
  (Syslog | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where SyslogMessage contains "看还能做什么" | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname = Computer, ActorUsername = ProcessName, CmdLine = SyslogMessage, ParentCmdLine = "", Source = "Syslog")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] .pgpass read followed by parallel SSH burst to internal host Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects the PostgreSQL-exfil chain: a process reads ~/.pgpass (the per-user libpq password file, source of the reused DB password) then within 10 minutes the same user/host opens 5+ short SSH sessions to a single downstream target — the 'eight short SSH sessions against a downstream SSH bastion server' pattern Sysdig described for the under-2-minute PostgreSQL dump. Rationale: Targets the article's lateral-move pivot: 'eight parallel SSH sessions against the downstream server to siphon an internal PostgreSQL database' driven by credentials extracted from .pgpass. The .pgpass-read seed is article-specific (Sysdig explicitly named running cat of ~/.pgpass to harvest the DB password); SSH-burst alone is too noisy, but anchored on a prior .pgpass cat by the same user within 10m, this catches the exact chain without flagging Ansible runs (which use known_hosts, not .pgpass). Cross-checked against: • https://webflow.sysdig.com/blog/ai-agent-at-the-wheel-how-an-attacker-used-llms-to-move-from-a-cve-to-an-internal-database-in-4-pivots
ATT&CKT1021.004 T1552.001 T1213
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowMinutes = 10;
let MinSshCount = 5;
let PgpassReads = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where FileName in~ ("cat","head","less","more","awk","grep","tail")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has ".pgpass"
    | project PgpassTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, PgpassUser = AccountName, PgpassCmd = ProcessCommandLine;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where FileName =~ "ssh"
| join kind=inner PgpassReads on DeviceId
| where AccountName == PgpassUser
| where Timestamp between (PgpassTime .. PgpassTime + WindowMinutes * 1m)
| summarize SshCount = count(),
            FirstSsh = min(Timestamp),
            LastSsh = max(Timestamp),
            BurstSeconds = datetime_diff('second', max(Timestamp), min(Timestamp)),
            SshCommands = make_set(ProcessCommandLine, 10)
        by DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, PgpassTime, PgpassCmd
| where SshCount >= MinSshCount
| order by FirstSsh desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowMinutes = 10;
let MinSshCount = 5;
let PgpassReads = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ActingProcessName in~ ("cat","head","less","more","awk","grep","tail")
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has ".pgpass"
    | project PgpassTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, PgpassUser = ActorUsername, PgpassCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ActingProcessName =~ "ssh"
| join kind=inner PgpassReads on DvcHostname
| where ActorUsername == PgpassUser
| where TimeGenerated between (PgpassTime .. PgpassTime + WindowMinutes * 1m)
| summarize SshCount = count(),
            FirstSsh = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSsh = max(TimeGenerated),
            BurstSeconds = datetime_diff('second', max(TimeGenerated), min(TimeGenerated)),
            SshCommands = make_set(ActingProcessCommandLine, 10)
        by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, PgpassTime, PgpassCmd
| where SshCount >= MinSshCount
| order by FirstSsh desc
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.name:(cat OR head OR less OR more OR awk OR grep) @process.command_line:*".pgpass"*
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\/(cat|head|less|more|awk|grep|tail)$/i CommandLine=/\.pgpass/
| pgpass_time := _time
| join({#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\/ssh$/}, field=[aid, UserName], include=[ssh_time:=_time, ssh_cmd:=CommandLine])
| delta := ssh_time - pgpass_time
| delta >= 0
| delta <= 600
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, pgpass_time], function={ count() | collect([ssh_cmd]) })
| _count >= 5
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` min(_time) as pgpass_time values(Processes.process) as pgpass_cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("cat","head","less","more","awk","grep") AND Processes.process="*.pgpass*" by host Processes.user | join type=inner host Processes.user [| tstats `summariesonly` count as ssh_count dc(Processes.process) as distinct_ssh values(Processes.process) as ssh_cmds min(_time) as first_ssh max(_time) as last_ssh from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="ssh" by host Processes.user] | eval delta = first_ssh - pgpass_time | where delta >= 0 AND delta <= 600 AND ssh_count >= 5 | table host Processes.user pgpass_time pgpass_cmd first_ssh last_ssh ssh_count distinct_ssh ssh_cmds
| tstats summariesonly=false min(_time) as pgpass_time values(Processes.process) as pgpass_cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("cat","head","less","more","awk","grep") AND Processes.process="*.pgpass*" by host Processes.user | join type=inner host Processes.user [| tstats summariesonly=false count as ssh_count dc(Processes.process) as distinct_ssh values(Processes.process) as ssh_cmds min(_time) as first_ssh max(_time) as last_ssh from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="ssh" by host Processes.user] | eval delta = first_ssh - pgpass_time | where delta >= 0 AND delta <= 600 AND ssh_count >= 5 | table host Processes.user pgpass_time pgpass_cmd first_ssh last_ssh ssh_count distinct_ssh ssh_cmds

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |

    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child

    - Legitimate automation macros in trusted internal documents
level: high

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine

SecurityEvent

| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Endpoint DNS/HTTP contact with seized Asocks/PROXYLIB C2 infrastructure · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
[LLM] Endpoint DNS/HTTP contact with seized Asocks/PROXYLIB C2 infrastructure Command & Control High
Retro-hunts (and goes-forward alerts) any host in the estate that resolved or connected to the three domains tied to the Dutch-seized 17M-device residential-proxy botnet: asocks.com, bproxy.one, lumiapps.io. A hit means the device is — or was — enrolled as a residential proxy exit node by the PROXYLIB/Asocks operator and likely shipped with a stealth proxyware SDK. Rationale: Three domains (asocks.com, bproxy.one, lumiapps.io) were pre-extracted from the article as the seized infrastructure's customer-facing fronts; the LumiApps SDK and bproxy.one are corroborated by the public Lumen/HUMAN PROXYLIB write-ups (proxylib/asocks SDK family). A retro-hunt across DNS + proxy + EDR network telemetry is the only durable signal because the malware ships as a stealth SDK embedded in legitimate-looking apps and exposes no other host-side IOCs. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1090/002/ • https://blog.lumen.com/proxylib-and-lumiapps-when-bonus-features-become-the-payload/ • https://www.humansecurity.com/learn/blog/satori-threat-intelligence-alert-badbox-and-peachpit-and-the-fraudulent-device-in-your-home
ATT&CKT1090.002 T1071.001 T1583.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let SeizedC2 = dynamic(["asocks.com","bproxy.one","lumiapps.io"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (SeizedC2)
    or RemoteUrl endswith ".asocks.com"
    or RemoteUrl endswith ".bproxy.one"
    or RemoteUrl endswith ".lumiapps.io"
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Hits=count(),
            Processes=make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, 25),
            CmdLines=make_set(InitiatingProcessCommandLine, 10),
            RemoteIPs=make_set(RemoteIP, 25)
          by DeviceId, DeviceName, RemoteUrl
| order by LastSeen desc
let SeizedC2 = dynamic(["asocks.com","bproxy.one","lumiapps.io"]);
union isfuzzy=true
 (DnsEvents
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
   | where Name has_any (SeizedC2)
   | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, ClientIP, QueryName=Name, QueryType=QueryTypeName, Source="DnsEvents"),
 (CommonSecurityLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
   | where DestinationHostName has_any (SeizedC2)
        or RequestURL has_any (SeizedC2)
        or DestinationDnsDomain has_any (SeizedC2)
   | project TimeGenerated, Host=SourceHostName, ClientIP=SourceIP, QueryName=coalesce(DestinationHostName, DestinationDnsDomain, RequestURL), QueryType=ApplicationProtocol, Source=strcat(DeviceVendor,":",DeviceProduct)),
 (ImDnsActivity
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
   | where DnsQuery has_any (SeizedC2)
   | project TimeGenerated, Host=coalesce(SrcHostname, DvcHostname), ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, QueryName=DnsQuery, QueryType=DnsQueryTypeName, Source="ImDnsActivity")
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Hits=count(),
            ClientIPs=make_set(ClientIP, 25), Sources=make_set(Source, 10)
          by Host, QueryName
| order by LastSeen desc

Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] GREYVIBE DroneLink WireGuard tunnel install on user workstation · [LLM] GREYVIBE network egress to known C2 IP infrastructure · [LLM] GREYVIBE LegionRelay RDP enablement and outbound 3389 from user endpoint · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] GREYVIBE LegionRelay browser, Telegram and WhatsApp data harvest · [LLM] GREYVIBE XMRig miner deployment on LegionRelay-infected host · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] GREYVIBE ClickFix fake Zoom/LAPAS CAPTCHA paste into Win+R then PowerShell Delivery High
Hunts the ClickFix initial-access pattern where a user lands on a fake Zoom/LAPAS CAPTCHA page (zoomconference.click/.app, lapas.live) and is coached to paste an attacker-supplied command into the Run dialog, spawning powershell.exe or mshta.exe from explorer.exe. This is GREYVIBE's documented entry path for the PhantomRelay/LegionRelay infection chain. Rationale: Article explicitly names zoomconference.click/.app and lapas.live as the ClickFix CAPTCHA domains, and the kill-chain phase-2 detection hint calls out explorer→powershell/mshta with Win+R paste indicators. The parent=explorer + suspicious cradle string + 5-minute proximity to a lure-domain visit on the same device is high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/002/ • https://www.proofpoint.com/us/blog/threat-insight/clickfix-malware-campaign-attack
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "explorer.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("iex ","Invoke-Expression","DownloadString","FromBase64String","-EncodedCommand","-enc ","-W Hidden","-WindowStyle Hidden","curl ","Invoke-RestMethod")
| join kind=leftouter (DeviceNetworkEvents | where Timestamp > ago(7d) | where RemoteUrl has_any ("zoomconference.click","zoomconference.app","lapas.live") | project DeviceId, ClickTime=Timestamp, BadUrl=RemoteUrl) on DeviceId
| where isnull(ClickTime) or Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 5m)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ParentImage=InitiatingProcessFolderPath, ChildImage=FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, BadUrl, ClickTime
| order by Timestamp desc
let LureDomains = dynamic(["zoomconference.click","zoomconference.app","lapas.live","strip-mens.tilda.ws"]);
let Visits = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where Url has_any (LureDomains)
    | project ClickTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, Url;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\explorer.exe"
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","\\mshta.exe","\\wscript.exe","\\cscript.exe")
| where CommandLine has_any ("iex ","Invoke-Expression","DownloadString","FromBase64String","-EncodedCommand","-enc ","-W Hidden","-WindowStyle Hidden","curl ","Invoke-RestMethod")
| join kind=leftouter Visits on $left.Computer == $right.DvcHostname
| where isnull(ClickTime) or TimeGenerated between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 5m)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, Url, ClickTime

[LLM] GREYVIBE PhantomMail Google Drive / 4sync archive lure delivered via email Delivery Medium
Detects inbound email containing links to Google Drive or 4sync that resolve to ZIP/RAR archives, which is GREYVIBE's PhantomMail spear-phishing delivery for JavaScript-based loaders that drop a decoy document and launch PhantomRelay. Correlates the email URL with subsequent archive extraction and JS execution on the recipient host. Rationale: Article specifies that PhantomMail emails carried links to Google Drive and 4sync archives containing JavaScript loaders, and the kill chain identifies wscript/cscript from extracted archive paths as the execution pivot. Correlating the email-side IOC (cloud-archive URLs) with the host-side JS-loader execution within a 6h window cuts FPs from legitimate file-share usage. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/002/
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes
let SuspiciousUrls = EmailUrlInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where Url has_any ("drive.google.com","4sync.com","4shared.com")
    | where Url has_any (".zip",".rar","download","uc?id=","file/d/");
let Recipients = EmailEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where DeliveryAction in ("Delivered","DeliveredAsSpam")
    | join kind=inner SuspiciousUrls on NetworkMessageId
    | project EmailTime=Timestamp, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress, Subject, Url, NetworkMessageId;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (".js",".jse",".vbs",".wsf")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\Downloads\",@"\Temp\",@"\AppData\Local\Temp\",@"\7-Zip\",@"\WinRAR\")
| join kind=inner (Recipients) on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| where Timestamp between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 6h)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountUpn, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Url, Subject, SenderFromAddress
let SuspectUrls = dynamic(["drive.google.com","4sync.com","4shared.com"]);
let Recips = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where Operation in ("MailItemsAccessed","Send")
    | extend Url = tostring(parse_json(Parameters))
    | where Url has_any (SuspectUrls) and Url has_any (".zip",".rar","file/d/","uc?id=")
    | project EmailTime=TimeGenerated, RecipientEmailAddress=UserId, Url;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\\wscript.exe","\\cscript.exe")
| where CommandLine has_any (".js",".jse",".vbs",".wsf")
| where CommandLine has_any ("\\Downloads\\","\\Temp\\","\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\")
| join kind=inner Recips on $left.TargetUserName == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 6h)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, TargetUserName, CommandLine, NewProcessName, ParentProcessName, Url
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\\wscript.exe OR *\\WScript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\CScript.exe) @CommandLine:(*.js* OR *.jse* OR *.vbs* OR *.wsf*) @CommandLine:(*\\Downloads\\* OR *\\Temp\\* OR *\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/(wscript|cscript)\.exe$/i
| regex("\\.(js|jse|vbs|wsf)", field=CommandLine)
| regex("\\\\(Downloads|Temp|AppData\\\\Local\\\\Temp)\\\\", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())

| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Email.All_Email where (All_Email.url="*drive.google.com/*" OR All_Email.url="*4sync.com/*" OR All_Email.url="*4shared.com/*") (All_Email.url="*.zip*" OR All_Email.url="*.rar*" OR All_Email.url="*download*" OR All_Email.url="*uc?id=*") by All_Email.recipient All_Email.src_user All_Email.subject All_Email.url | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
[LLM] GREYVIBE PhantomRelayV1 watchdog persistence via Run key or scheduled task Installation Medium
Detects the PhantomRelayV1 'custom watchdog' persistence pattern — a paired powershell.exe process that immediately re-spawns a sibling powershell.exe within seconds of termination, registered via a Run/RunOnce key or a scheduled task. This is GREYVIBE's documented mechanism to keep the PowerShell RAT alive across reboots and termination. Rationale: Article calls out PhantomRelayV1's 'custom watchdog persistence mechanism' and kill-chain phase 3 specifies Run/RunOnce keys plus paired sibling re-spawn within seconds. The combination of Run-key registration of a hidden-window powershell + a 5-minute window with ≥2 sibling powershell spawns from a parent powershell is the watchdog fingerprint. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1547/001/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
ATT&CKT1547.001 T1053.005 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry Endpoint.Processes
let RunKeyPersist = DeviceRegistryEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
    | where RegistryKey has_any (@"\CurrentVersion\Run",@"\CurrentVersion\RunOnce")
    | where RegistryValueData has_any ("powershell","pwsh")
    | where RegistryValueData has_any ("-W Hidden","-WindowStyle Hidden","-EncodedCommand","-enc ","hidden","Start-Job","-NoP","-NonI")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData, InitiatingProcessFileName;
let WatchdogSpawn = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
    | where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Start-Job","Start-Process","-WindowStyle Hidden","While","watchdog")
    | summarize Spawns=count(), arg_min(Timestamp,*) by DeviceName, AccountName, bin(Timestamp, 5m)
    | where Spawns >= 2;
RunKeyPersist
| join kind=leftouter (WatchdogSpawn | project DeviceName, WatchdogTime=Timestamp, Spawns) on DeviceName
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData, WatchdogTime, Spawns
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where RegistryKey has_any ("\\CurrentVersion\\Run","\\CurrentVersion\\RunOnce")
| where RegistryValueData has_any ("powershell","pwsh")
| where RegistryValueData has_any ("-W Hidden","-WindowStyle Hidden","-EncodedCommand","-enc ","hidden","Start-Job","-NoP","-NonI","watchdog")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName
| join kind=leftouter (
    ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where ParentProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("Start-Job","Start-Process","-WindowStyle Hidden","watchdog")
    | summarize Spawns=count(), WatchdogTime=min(TimeGenerated) by DvcHostname, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
    | where Spawns >= 2
) on DvcHostname

[LLM] GREYVIBE LegionRelay browser, Telegram and WhatsApp data harvest Actions on Objectives High
Hunts LegionRelay's credential and messenger data theft by alerting on powershell.exe (or unsigned binaries) opening Chrome/Edge/Firefox 'Login Data' and 'Cookies' SQLite files, %AppData%\Telegram Desktop\tdata, and WhatsApp local storage. These exact targets are listed in the article as LegionRelay capabilities. Rationale: Article lists LegionRelay capabilities verbatim: 'browser data theft, Telegram and WhatsApp data exfiltration', and kill-chain phase 6 specifies Chrome/Edge/Firefox 'Login Data' + 'Cookies' SQLite + tdata + WhatsApp local storage as the file targets. Combined with non-browser proc reading those paths, this is high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
ATT&CKT1555.003 T1539 T1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
   or FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",@"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",@"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\",@"\Telegram Desktop\tdata\",@"\WhatsApp\")
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",@"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",@"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\",@"\Telegram Desktop\tdata\",@"\WhatsApp\")
   or FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","key4.db","key3.db")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","cmd.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName == ""
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","telegram.exe","whatsapp.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let TargetPaths = dynamic(["\\Google\\Chrome\\User Data\\","\\Microsoft\\Edge\\User Data\\","\\Mozilla\\Firefox\\Profiles\\","\\Telegram Desktop\\tdata\\","\\WhatsApp\\"]);
let TargetFiles = dynamic(["Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","key4.db","key3.db"]);
let LegitBrowserProcs = dynamic(["chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","telegram.exe","whatsapp.exe"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFilePath has_any (TargetPaths) or TargetFileName in~ (TargetFiles)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","cmd.exe")
| where not (ActingProcessName has_any (LegitBrowserProcs))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, Hash

[LLM] GREYVIBE DroneLink WireGuard tunnel install on user workstation Command & Control High
Detects DroneLink chain installing a WireGuard tunnel (wireguard.exe / wg.exe / tunnel.dll service) on a user workstation — the article cites fake Ukrainian-Armed-Forces charity sites delivering WireGuard and LegionRelay. Workstations almost never legitimately install ad-hoc WireGuard interfaces. Rationale: Article specifies DroneLink delivers WireGuard plus LegionRelay via charity-impersonation sites; kill-chain phase 8 calls out WireGuard tunnels from user endpoints as a high-fidelity C2 signal. Workstations rarely legitimately receive ad-hoc WireGuard installs, and excluding MSI/Intune/SCCM parents removes the corporate VPN deployment baseline. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1572/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1219/
ATT&CKT1572 T1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
let WgProcs = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where FileName in~ ("wireguard.exe","wg.exe","wg-quick.exe")
       or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("WireGuard","tunnel.dll","/installtunnelservice","wg-quick")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msiexec.exe","setup.exe","intunemanagementextension.exe","ccmexec.exe")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256;
let WgFiles = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where FileName in~ ("wireguard.exe","wg.exe","tunnel.dll") or FolderPath has @"\WireGuard\"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
union WgProcs, WgFiles
| order by Timestamp desc
let WgFileNames = dynamic(["wireguard.exe","wg.exe","wg-quick.exe","tunnel.dll"]);
let ShellProcs = dynamic(["powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe"]);
let WgProcs = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where ActingProcessName has_any (WgFileNames)
        or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("WireGuard","tunnel.dll","/installtunnelservice","wg-quick")
    | where not (ParentProcessName has_any ("msiexec.exe","setup.exe","intunemanagementextension.exe","ccmexec.exe"))
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName;
let WgFiles = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where TargetFileName has_any (WgFileNames) or TargetFilePath has "\\WireGuard\\"
    | where ActingProcessName has_any (ShellProcs)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName;
WgProcs
| union WgFiles
| order by TimeGenerated desc

references:

[LLM] GREYVIBE network egress to known C2 IP infrastructure Command & Control High
Alerts on any outbound connection from an endpoint to the 8 GREYVIBE C2 IPs documented in the WithSecure write-up. These IPs were used for PhantomRelay/LegionRelay beaconing and file exfiltration; any hit warrants immediate triage. Rationale: All 8 IPs are pulled verbatim from the IOC bundle in the kill-chain reconstruction and named as PhantomRelay/LegionRelay C2/exfil infrastructure (phases 8-9). Any organisational endpoint touching any of these IPs is a direct article-grounded IOC hit. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
let C2 = dynamic(["188.124.59.120","193.233.23.81","89.37.185.60","74.112.102.120","194.87.128.243","194.87.108.110","89.125.189.118","89.125.189.85"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (C2)
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Conns=count(),
            Procs=make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, 10),

[LLM] GREYVIBE LegionRelay RDP enablement and outbound 3389 from user endpoint Command & Control High
Detects LegionRelay's RDP-access-setup behaviour: registry change enabling Terminal Services (fDenyTSConnections=0) and/or firewall rule allowing RDP, followed by outbound TCP/3389 from a workstation that normally does not initiate RDP. Article explicitly lists 'RDP access setup' as a LegionRelay capability. Rationale: Article calls out 'RDP access setup' as a LegionRelay capability; the standard mechanism is flipping fDenyTSConnections=0 plus a firewall allow rule. Pairing the registry change with a netsh/PowerShell firewall command in the same hour, on a workstation, is high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/001/
ATT&CKT1021.001 T1112 T1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry Endpoint.Processes
let RdpEnable = DeviceRegistryEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where (RegistryKey has @"\Terminal Server" and RegistryValueName =~ "fDenyTSConnections" and RegistryValueData == "0")
         or (RegistryKey has @"\WinStations\RDP-Tcp" and RegistryValueName =~ "UserAuthentication")
    | project RegTime=Timestamp, DeviceName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
let FwRule = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where (FileName =~ "netsh.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "Remote Desktop")
         or (FileName =~ "powershell.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Set-NetFirewallRule -DisplayGroup \"Remote Desktop\"","Enable-NetFirewallRule"))
    | project FwTime=Timestamp, DeviceName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName;
RdpEnable
| join kind=leftouter FwRule on DeviceName
| where isnull(FwTime) or FwTime between (RegTime - 1h .. RegTime + 1h)
| project RegTime, DeviceName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueData, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FwTime, FwCmd=ProcessCommandLine
let RdpEnable = ImRegistryEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where (RegistryKey has "\\Terminal Server" and RegistryValue =~ "fDenyTSConnections" and RegistryValueData == "0")
         or (RegistryKey has "\\WinStations\\RDP-Tcp" and RegistryValue =~ "UserAuthentication")
    | project RegTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine;
let FwRule = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where (ActingProcessName has "netsh.exe" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "Remote Desktop")
         or (ActingProcessName has "powershell.exe" and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("Set-NetFirewallRule","Enable-NetFirewallRule"))
    | project FwTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActingProcessCommandLine;
RdpEnable
| join kind=leftouter FwRule on DvcHostname
| where isnull(FwTime) or FwTime between (RegTime - 1h .. RegTime + 1h)

[LLM] GREYVIBE princess-club and Zoom/LAPAS lookalike domain access Reconnaissance High
Hunts inbound or outbound web traffic to the lure domains GREYVIBE used across PhantomClick, PrincessClub and Nebo: zoomconference.click/.app, lapas.live, strip-mens.tilda.ws, princess-mens.fun/.click/.com, princessclub.click. Captures both the initial-access click and any WebRTC AV-capture follow-on. Rationale: Article and IOC bundle name every one of these domains as lures used in PhantomClick (Zoom/LAPAS), PrincessClub (princess-* / strip-mens) and related chains. Any organisational endpoint resolving or visiting these is a direct article-grounded IOC hit; resolution covers the WebRTC-AV-capture flow as well. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/002/
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1583.001 T1204.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web

let NetHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where RemoteUrl has_any (LureDomains)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP;
let UrlHits = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where Url has_any (LureDomains)
    | project Timestamp, AccountUpn, Url, ActionType, IPAddress, IsClickedThrough;

| union (UrlHits | extend DeviceName="<email-click>", InitiatingProcessAccountName=AccountUpn, RemoteUrl=Url, RemoteIP=IPAddress)
| order by Timestamp desc

    | where Url has_any (LureDomains) or HttpHostName has_any (LureDomains)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Url, HttpHostName;
let DnsHits = ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DnsQuery has_any (LureDomains)

WebHits
| union DnsHits

[LLM] GREYVIBE XMRig miner deployment on LegionRelay-infected host Actions on Objectives High
Detects XMRig command-line invocation (stratum+tcp, --donate-level, -o, --tls-fingerprint) on an endpoint, which the article notes GREYVIBE deploys on a subset of LegionRelay-infected machines for monetisation alongside espionage. The combination of mining-pool C2 strings on a normally-non-mining host is high-fidelity. Rationale: Article phase-10 detection hint specifies XMRig command-line flags (-o, --donate-level, stratum+tcp) and mining pool connections. These strings are mining-specific and almost never appear in legitimate enterprise software on a user workstation. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1496/ • https://github.com/xmrig/xmrig
ATT&CKT1496
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("stratum+tcp","stratum+ssl","--donate-level","--randomx","-o pool.","--tls-fingerprint","xmrig")
   or FileName =~ "xmrig.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("stratum+tcp","stratum+ssl","--donate-level","--randomx","-o pool.","--tls-fingerprint","xmrig")
   or ActingProcessName =~ "xmrig.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, SHA256

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
